title: Cross-model Evaluation Suite and Scheduling Guidelines
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:
This document defines the cross-model evaluation suite (aka the CrossEval Suite), a deterministic matrix of tests and an operational scheduling policy used by the eval-harness to run routine and ad-hoc evaluations against hosted and dedicated model variants. It covers: the evaluation matrix design, prompt perturbation families, resource-aware scheduling, pass/fail SLOs, CI/CD integration, and an incident/runbook for failed or noisy runs.

Intended audience:
- ML engineers onboarding models to Redwood serving
- Applied ML and Evals team owners
- Platform and SRE engineers who operate the eval infrastructure

Goals and success criteria:
- Detect functional regressions and quality drift with >=95% sensitivity for prioritized prompt-sets within 24 hours of a deployment.
- Maintain median eval-turnaround <= 30 minutes for smoke batches and <= 6 hours for full CrossEval runs.
- Keep eval cost within budgeted allocation (default: 1.2% of monthly Dedicated GPU hours per model candidate).

1) CrossEval Suite structure:
- Matrix axes: model_variant x prompt_family x metric_group x compute_profile
- Model_variant: {baseline (golden), candidate (new commit), quantized-variant, fallback-variant}
- Prompt_family (examples): conversational_flow, instruction-following, code-transformation, safety-edgecases, slot-filling, numeric-reasoning
- Metric_group: accuracy-like (F1/EM), calibration (ECE), factuality (fact-check pass rate), toxicity (safety gating), output-length/efficiency (avg tokens), latency (p50/p95 generation)
- Compute_profile: cpu-smoke, small-gpu (T4/RTX A10), large-gpu (A100/H100)

Table: example minimal CrossEval matrix (rendered here as pipe table)
| prompt_family | metric_primary | smoke | full | quantized_check | notes |
| conversational_flow | E2E-conv-coherence (BLEU/ROUGE-lite) | x | x | x | include prefix caching test |
| code-transformation | functional-pass@1 | x | x | x | run on deterministic seed sets |
| safety-edgecases | safety-block-rate | x | x | x | include adversarial perturbations |

2) Prompt perturbation and stress families:
- Canonical prompt set: the curated canonical prompts for each family (stored in /datasets/evals/canonical-prompts).
- Perturbation families (applied per canonical prompt):
  - Tokenization_shifts: insert/remove punctuation, whitespace variants
  - Role_swap: swap 'assistant' and 'user' role markers to detect role-dependence
  - Data-slice-sampling: stratified sampling for rare tokens, numerics, and long-context cases
  - Adversarial-noise: paraphrase and synonym substitution up to 20% token change
- For each canonical prompt we generate up to 12 perturbations in smoke runs and 60 for full runs.

3) Metrics, thresholds, and SLOs:
- Regression detection SLOs (per-run):
  - Quality delta alert: any candidate model with drop >= 3.0% absolute on primary metric for a prompt_family triggers 'regression-alert'.
  - Statistical significance: use paired bootstrap with 1000 resamples; require p <= 0.05 to escalate automatic regression.
- Operational SLOs (infrastructure):
  - Smoke run median completion: <= 30 minutes (target)
  - Full CrossEval completion: <= 6 hours (target)
  - Eval-job error rate: <= 0.5% per day
- Alerting thresholds:
  - If more than 5 prompt_families report degradation or any safety-block-rate increases by >=1 percentage point, auto-notify #ml-evals and create a regression incident in the tracker.

4) Scheduling policy and resource-aware placement:
- Priority levels:
  - P0: Canary / pre-production candidate that will be rolled automatically if passes (highest priority)
  - P1: Nightly full CrossEval runs for all committed variants
  - P2: Ad-hoc exploratory runs or long tail stress-bench jobs
- Scheduler behavior (eval-scheduler service):
  - Resource-aware packing: group similar compute_profile runs to enable shared KV cache warm-starting across model variants.
  - Rate-limited burst windows: allow P0 runs to preempt P1 only within configured maintenance windows (default 02:00-06:00 UTC).
  - Backoff policy: failed jobs use exponential backoff up to 4 retries before filing a failed-eval ticket.
- Example priorities mapping:
  - Canary (commit to main): P0 -> prefer small-gpu, dedicate 1 slot per model by default
  - Nightly: P1 -> batch multiple model variants together to amortize prefix cache costs

5) Integration with CI/CD and Canary rollout:
- When a model is pushed to 'candidate' registry tag, CI triggers a smoke CrossEval (P0). The pipeline steps:
  1) create eval-runner job via eval-cli run --suite=crosseval --variant=candidate --profile=small-gpu --priority=P0
  2) monitor job stream and metrics; fail the CI if primary metric drop >= 3% and p <= 0.05
  3) on pass, attach evaluation report to build artifact and allow automated canary rollout to 5% traffic
- CLI examples:
  - Start smoke: eval-cli run --suite=crosseval --variant=candidate --profile=small-gpu --prompt-set=smoke --notify-channel=#ml-evals
  - Query results: eval-cli fetch --job-id=<job> --format=summary|json

6) Runbook: noisy, partial, or failed runs
- Symptoms and initial checks:
  - High variance between repeated smoke runs (>5x std-dev on primary metric) -> check randomness seed and dataset partitioning
  - Spikes in per-instance latency or OOMs -> check instance logs (eval-runner/<job-id>/stderr), GPU memory footprint, and kernel selection hints
- Triage steps (ordered):
  1) Reproduce: re-run smoke set with deterministic flag --seed=20250101 and profile small-gpu
  2) Compare: fetch baseline run and compute delta via eval-cli diff --base=<golden> --candidate=<job>
  3) Isolation: run targeted prompt_family (e.g., code-transformation drought) to localize regression
  4) Infrastructure: if OOM or kernel failure, escalate to eng-serving-runtime on-call and attach metrics trace id
  5) Root cause: file regression incident and assign to applied-ml owner with a remediation ETA
- Post-incident steps: update canonical prompts if false-positive due to prompt obsolescence; add new perturbation seed to avoid recurrence.

7) Cost controls and amortization strategies:
- Batching policy: when running nightlies, bin model variants that share the same tokenizer and architecture to reuse tokenizer load costs and KV warm caches.
- Quantized checks: heavy quantized regression tests use reduced prompt samples (20% of full) but include all adversarial perturbations to detect precision-sensitive failures.
- Budget alert: spend >120% of monthly eval-hours triggers finance-notification and pauses low-priority P2 jobs.

8) Dashboards and reporting:
- Primary dashboards: eval-cross-suite-overview (per-model variant), crosseval-regressions (alerts & incidents), cost-by-suite.
- Required dashboard widgets: median primary metric trend, prompt_family heatmap (delta per family), per-run latency histogram, bootstrap significance summary.
- Report cadence:
  - Daily: smoke-run summary to #ml-evals at 09:00 UTC
  - Weekly: top-5 regressions report to eng-leads

9) Ownership and rollout checklist for new models:
- Pre-onboarding: ensure model card includes architecture, supported max_seq_len, quantization compatibility, and expected batch vs streaming throughput.
- Onboarding steps (numbered):
  1) Add model metadata to registry and mark 'golden' baseline if available
  2) Create canonical prompt mapping for each prompt_family (store in /datasets/evals/canonical-prompts/<model>)
  3) Run initial CrossEval smoke (P0) and confirm no safety-block regressions
  4) Schedule nightly full CrossEval for 3 days; review and sign-off by applied-ml owner

Appendix A: sample eval job YAML (example used by eval-scheduler)

# sample_job.yaml
name: crosseval-candidate-2026-02
suite: crosseval
variant: candidate-v3
prompt_sets: [smoke, stress-adversarial]
compute_profile: small-gpu
priority: P0
interruptible: false
max_retries: 4
notify: ["#ml-evals", "integrations/eval-reports"]

Appendix B: common CLI snippets
- List available suites: eval-cli list-suites
- Submit a full-night run (example):
  eval-cli run --suite=crosseval --variant=candidate-v3 --profile=large-gpu --prompt-set=full --priority=P1 --notify-channel=#ml-evals

Appendix C: glossary of service names referenced
- eval-scheduler: service that queues and assigns eval jobs to available compute pools
- eval-runner: per-instance worker that executes prompts against target model binaries and emits metrics/traces
- redwood-observability: metrics/tracing dashboarding stack (Prometheus/Grafana + traces)
